stories.head: Vast aims for defense contracts with new division
stories.body: Vast has launched a new division specifically for national security projects, signaling a strategic pivot towards the defense sector. This move comes as companies like True Anomaly secure $190 million in Series C funding, showcasing the government's growing appetite for co-orbital security solutions. Vast's initiative reflects a broader trend where space companies are eager to tap into the lucrative defense market, previously dominated by traditional contractors.
stories.soWhat: If Vast can land defense contracts, it might just validate the notion that every space company should have a 'defense' wing.

stories.head: Relativity Space ramps up Terran R production
stories.body: Relativity Space is expanding its Terran R production capabilities in Florida, aiming to capitalize on the growing demand for launch services. This expansion comes on the heels of a $260 million Series C funding round for Stoke Space, also focused on reusable launch systems. With the launch market heating up, Relativity's increased production could position it as a key player in the medium-lift category.
stories.soWhat: In a crowded field, the ability to scale quickly might just be the ticket to staying relevant—assuming they can actually launch on time.

stories.head: Anduril and L3Harris team for SDA constellation
stories.body: Anduril and L3Harris are joining forces to bid on a tactical Space Development Agency (SDA) constellation, highlighting the growing trend of collaboration in defense tech. Their partnership aims to leverage L3Harris's satellite expertise alongside Anduril's innovative defense capabilities. As the FY27 budget adds $1.4 billion for space resilience, this collaboration could be a timely move to secure government contracts amid increasing competition.
stories.soWhat: In defense contracting, partnerships can be more valuable than solo acts; it's all about who you know—and who you can convince to join you.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on True Anomaly's momentum
watchlist.body: With $190 million in fresh funding, True Anomaly could expand its influence in co-orbital security, potentially attracting more government contracts.

watchlist.title: Watch for Sierra Space's next moves
watchlist.body: Having cleared a critical design review, Sierra Space's Dream Chaser DoD variant could soon be on the launch pad—if it ever gets there.

watchlist.title: Relativity's production timeline matters
watchlist.body: As Relativity ramps up production, any delays could impact its competitiveness in the increasingly crowded launch market.

watchlist.title: Expect more from the Defense-Tech IPO window
watchlist.body: With signs of life in defense-tech IPOs, investors might start looking for the next big thing beyond the usual suspects.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
